ov: A slender, long-legged wild cat with a reddish-tan coat and long black ear tufts; its name comes from the Turkish for "black ear". It lives alone or in pairs, hunts mostly at night, and prefers dry country.
len: Males 78–108 cm, females 71–103 cm (head and body)
rg: Africa, the Middle East and Central Asia, to arid parts of Pakistan and northwestern India.
df: Mostly small mammals, plus birds, small monkeys and young antelopes.

cf.tip: The serval has no ear tufts, a spotted coat, longer legs and a longer tail.

fx: Mughal emperors in India used caracals to hunt game birds.
Betting on caracals killing pigeons in an arena probably gave us the phrase "to put the cat among the pigeons".
notes: The animals.js fact is confirmed: it can leap higher than 3 m and catch birds in midair.
